blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A shared `genericCalc(amount, rate, isTax)` picks one of two behaviours by its flag. Per this page, how is it fixed?

options.text: Move the flag's check into a base class that both behaviours extend
options.says: The page advises composition over inheritance for DRY, not a shared base class.

options.text: Inline it back into two separate methods, one for each behaviour
options.says: The page's fix inlines the wrong abstraction into separate methods that evolve independently.

options.text: Add one more flag for the next pricing rule that has to reuse it
options.says: The page names flag parameters as the sign of a wrong abstraction, not its cure.

questions.stem: `EmployeeAddress` and `CustomerAddress` have the same three fields. Per this page, why keep two records rather than one?

options.text: They belong to different domains, and each may change on its own
options.says: The page says separate records signal different domain types that may diverge.

options.text: A record cannot be used as a field type in two unrelated classes
options.says: The page gives type safety and independent evolution as the reasons, not a limit on records.

options.text: They represent the same concept, so each use needs its own record
options.says: The page says the opposite: if they truly represent the same concept, use one record for both.

concepts: Two records with the same fields but different domains stay separate types, so each can evolve on its own.
A wrong abstraction grows boolean flags and special cases, and is fixed by inlining it back into separate methods.
